answer: To raise sybil costs, each identity may lease only one exclusive work plot in a public orchard of long-horizon tasks. Plots sell in a sealed auction, cannot be split or moved for many epochs, and require a locked bond. Progress posts across a settlement bridge that peers recompute from the same seed; near-duplicate traces merge into one plot. Sanctions tighten on a velvet schedule: payout freeze, then a bond burn, then ejection. A farm must buy a new plot, lock new capital, and wait out calendar time for every extra identity, because cloned work shares one plot and cannot multiply rewards.
